## Learn how to improve your marketing — for free. Get the weekly newsletter keeping thousands of marketers in the loop. # 10 best newsletter platforms & software I'm using in 2026 Starting a newsletter is a great way to own your audience. Here are the best email newsletter platforms and software to help build your audience in 2026. Three years ago, I quit my tech job in San Francisco to start a media company. One of the core products of that media company was starting a newsletter. I had a vision for what I wanted my newsletter to be, a digital magazine. From text, images, links, interactive polls, GIFs, and more. I wanted to have a unique newsletter that people were excited to open and read. Inspired by some other newsletter companies, like The Hustle (that sold to HubSpot for $27 Million), I tired to find the best newsletter platforms that could enable me to do everything I wanted (from a feature perspective). I quickly came to realize that knowing what newsletter software to use can be tricky. And most newsletters with millions of subscribers actually use a custom tech stack that they create in-house. These custom solutions allow them to scale and track all of their newsletter metrics. But you don’t need a fancy tech stack to get started. In fact, some of the best newsletter platforms I listed below are used by newsletters with hundreds of thousands of subscribers. In this article, I plan on giving you a list of the best email newsletter software and the best email newsletter service options currently on the market. I'm writing this article from the perspective of how I would give a recommendation to my best friend. If you want the TL;DR of my top picks, here they are: Scroll below to see my personal opinion on each one (and the platform I chose for my own newsletter). I'll also highlight the best free newsletter platforms if you're just getting started. ## What is an email newsletter service? An email newsletter service is a SaaS (software as a service) solution that allows you to start and grow an email newsletter. They say the best way to make yourself algorithm proof is to start a newsletter . It’s important to own your own list that you can tap into at any moment. For example, it’s much more valuable to have an email list of 10,000 subscribers than it is to have 10,000 Twitter followers or YouTube subscribers. The goal of an email newsletter service is to allow creators to capture emails, whether it’s from social media or from their website, and let them communicate directly with their audience through the medium of email. Some creators also pair their newsletter platform with an AI writer to speed up content creation. However, not every email newsletter service is created equal. ## How to choose the best newsletter platform Finding the right email newsletter platform is important. With so many newsletter services available, it can feel overwhelming to pick the right one. And I wrote this article in a way that will truly help you discover the platform that is right for you. Most blog posts on this topic are either created by the company that created the newsletter platform, or by media websites with biased sponsored listings. I'm not sponsored by any of the platforms below. It’s a pure and honest overview of what I believe to be the best platforms for launching a newsletter. Here’s are some questions you should ask when looking for in a newsletter platform: - How many subscribers can you have on a free plan? - How easy is it to write and design a newsletter? - How much room is there for growth? - How much does it cost as your newsletter grows? - Does it have all the features you want for your newsletter experience? - Is there an intuitive dashboard for tracking your analytics? - How hard or easy is it to migrate off of? - Are there proper spam filters in place to make sure there is successful email deliverability? It’s a lot of questions to ask. But I tried to make sure that the platforms chosen in this list (in order) serve the right responses to these questions. Okay, enough of me rambling, let’s get into the list. ## 10 best newsletter platforms and software in 2026 Here are my top picks for the best newsletter platforms: - beehiiv - MailerLite - Kit - Flodesk - Ghost - Substack - Mailmodo - Aweber - Campaign Monitor - Mailchimp Let’s see which one is right for you. ### 1. beehiiv beehiiv is an all-in-one newsletter platform designed for creators who are serious about growth. The cool thing about beehiiv is that the founders of the tool were on the growth team at the Morning Brew — a popular business newsletter with millions of subscribers. beehiiv is free (up to 2,500 subscribers) and makes it easy to design, send, and scale your newsletter. They have a clean and minimal editor that makes it easy to craft emails, along with tools to help you track performance and subscriber growth. They also recently acquired Typedream, an AI website builder , which means you can now build a full website for your newsletter without writing any code. The drag-and-drop builder has templates, landing pages, and AI tools to help you create your site really fast. On their higher tier plans, you can get access to a referral program (that allows you to incentivize your readers to invite their friends) and paid subscriptions. These are great features that you don’t really see in a lot of other free newsletter

Free for up to 2,500 subscribers! ### 2. MailerLite MailerLite is an email marketing software and newsletter platform with over 1.4M users. At its core, MailerLite is a digital marketing and email tool. However, it does have a dedicated newsletter builder. There’s a beautiful drag-and-drop editor, along with a wide variety of newsletter templates to help you craft a clean and original newsletter design. MailerLite is a great tool to start your newsletter because it offers a generous free plan and gives you more than just newsletter functionality. You can also create a website, add sign up forms to existing websites, create a blog, and set up automations to new and existing email subscribers. If you’re a bit more technical savvy, you can even use MailerLite’s custom HTML email editor to build a completely custom newsletter design. MailerLite also has great analytics and reporting features. You can view everything from the number of subscribers you have, open rates, CTR (click through rates), who unsubscribed, and who marked your emails as spam. > “The pre-built email blocks are great and very easy to use so I can create beautiful visuals for newsletters to current and future parents of students of our school.” — Myriam Pagé MailerLite also boasts a 24/7 support service, making sure

unsubscribed, and who marked your emails as spam. > “The pre-built email blocks are great and very easy to use so I can create beautiful visuals for newsletters to current and future parents of students of our school.” — Myriam Pagé MailerLite also boasts a 24/7 support service, making sure that any and all of your questions can be answered at any time of the day. #### MailerLite pricing MailerLite’s pricing varies on the number of email subscribers you have. Here is what it looks like for 1,000 subscribers: You’ll have to adjust the slider on the subscriber count to get more accurate results. But here is what the pricing would come out to if we modeled the same number of subscribers listed in beehiiv’s pricing: - Free: $0/month, up to 1,000 subscribers, and includes drag-and-drop editor - Growing Business: $9/month (billed annually), starts at 1,000 subscribers, and sell digital products - Advance: $19/month (billed annually), starts at 1,000 subscribers, HTML editor, and automation builder features As you can see, the price is slightly higher than beehiiv . However, based on the features and the support that comes with MailerLite, it’s listed as the second best newsletter platform on our list. It’s still a lot cheaper than some of the other email newsletter software out there. #### MailerLite reviews - G2: 4.7/5 star rating ( +915 reviews ) - Capterra: 4.8/5 star rating ( +1,992 reviews ) ### 3. Kit Kit, formerly known as ConvertKit, is a popular email and newsletter platform for creators. Kit is used by a wide range of people, including independent writers, musicians, podcasters, online artists, coaches, and bloggers. They, like Substack, provide a paid newsletter function that allows you to charge users for a premium newsletter. Kit also offers a variety of email designs and business solutions, including automation tools, sales funnels, pop-ups, and landing pages to mention a few. Just like beehiiv, Kit also has a referral program — making it easy to incentivize your subscribers to help you grow. #### Kit pricing Compared to the other newsletter platforms on our list, Kit is a bit on the pricier side. Here are their pricing plans: Similar to MailerLite, Kit pricing varies on the number of subscribers you want on each plan. They have a slider you can use to compare plans for individual subscriber counts. Comparing pricing to beehiiv (first on our list), this is what it would look like: - Newsletter: $0/month, up to 10,000 subscribers, unlimited newsletter sending and forms - Creator: $9/month, starts at 300 subscribers, remove branding and include polls - Creator Pro: $50/month, starts at 1,000 subscribers, includes referral program - Enterprise: Custom/month, Unlimited everything, concierge onboarding If you have under 100,000 subscribers, Kit recommends that you use their Creator plan. If you like what Kit has to offer, but you're not completely sold yet, you can check out some other Kit alternatives . ### 4. Flodesk Flodesk is a modern newsletter platform designed for brands that are focused on selling. What makes Flodesk a bit different from other email services is that it focused on beautiful design. Their motto is “Today’s top brands have the best design. Now, so do you,” so it goes to show what their platform stands for. Flodesk can also seamlessly integrate with platforms like Shopify or WooCommerce, making lead generation and customer engagement more streamlined. Beyond its eye-pleasing email templates, it's renowned for its ease of use and powerful tools such as audience segmentation and anayltics. Whether you're an ecommerce veteran or a newbie, its user-friendly interface makes it easy to quickly create and send out effective campaigns. Using Zapier, you can also make Flodesk compatible with various plugins to enhance its functionality — making it a comprehensive tool for brands looking to send clean and modern email marketing campaigns. #### Flodesk pricing Flodesk has an interesting price plan that is not common among a lot of other email marketing tools, and I mean that in a good way. Here’s what the pricing looks like if you sign up for a monthly plan: Flodesk’s pricing models work based on what email marketing features you need. For example, if you just want email marketing features, plans start at $38/month. But if you want to create sales pages and sell products, you’ll have to upgrade. Check out Flodesk’s pricing plans: - Free: $0/month for unlimited subscribers (limited email sends) - Email: $38/month for unlimited email marketing features ‍ - Email + Checkout: $64/month for unlimited sales pages and ecommerce features For what you get, these prices are unmatched. And if you decide to pay annually upfront, you can expect 1 month of free service. ### 5. Ghost Originally created as a WordPress CMS (content management system) alternative for blogs, Ghost has evolved into a complete content and newsletter platform for creators. With the release of Ghost 5.0 , Ghost is now a platform for independent content creators. Besides beehiiv, this is probably one of the most promising newsletter platforms on my list. Ghost is a powerful app for media creators, allowing them to publish, share, and grow their content business. It's great if you want a newsletter website that combines your blog and email list in one place. The platform is extremely modern, gives you a full website, CMS, newsletter platform, and the ability to launch paid subscriptions. Ghost has been around since 2013, but their new refresh that’s dedicated to newsletter growth is quite intriguing (in a good way). If you don’t already have a website, and you plan on creating a blog, Ghost is a platform you seriously want to look into. Their CMS is extremely lightweight and fast, and their newsletter platform

If you don’t already have a website, and you plan on creating a blog, Ghost is a platform you seriously want to look into. Their CMS is extremely lightweight and fast, and their newsletter platform looks promising. They also have a minimal and clean design like beehiiv and make it easy to track all of your content metrics and analytics. You can also leverage paid subscriptions as an option to monetize your newsletter content. #### Ghost pricing Ghost has a free trial, but you’re going to have to pay to use it for the long-term. Their pricing is based on two variables: number of subscribers and desired feature set. Here is what their general pricing looks like: Pricing for Ghost is slightly more expensive than beehiiv or MailerLite, but it’s because you’re also getting a full CMS that can be used to publish blog posts on your website. If you have over 1,000 subscribers you’ll have to use either the Creator, Team, or Business plan — the Starter plan is limited to just 1,000 subscribers. For most creator’s creating a newsletter, you’ll probably want to use the “Creator” plan. Here’s what the Creator plan will look like for different subscriber counts: - Starter: $11/month for up to 5,000 subscribers - Creator: $31/month starting at 1,000 subscribers - Team: $63/month starting at 1,000 subscribers - Business: $249/month starting at 10,000 subscribers For what you get, this pricing is very reasonable. And it scales based on the number of subscribers you need. Think of each plan as a the feature set you get (but the price goes up with the number of members/subscribers you have. Ghost is great, especially as a CMS (one of my client's use them). But if you just need newsletter functionality, you’ll probably want to go with one of the newsletter platforms mentioned earlier. ### 6. Substack If you know anything about journalism and paid newsletters, you’ve probably heard of Substack. Substack has grown in popularity in the past few years. It’s a platform that makes it super easy to start a newsletter and start getting paid (if you decide to offer a premium subscription). Both beehiiv and MailerLite also offer paid subscription options, however what makes Substack different from other free newsletter platforms is that it's completely free to use. The only catch is that if you do have a paid subscription option, Substack will take a 10% revenue cut from what you make. If you have a lot of subscribers, this may actually end up costing you more compared to some other Substack alternatives like beehiiv. Regardless, Substack is a great newsletter platform if you just want to get started and get in the habit of writing to an audience. It’s really easy to search for other Substack publications, so there’s a chance that people may be able to discover your newsletter straight through Substack’s platform. However, if you want to

However, if you want to have your own dedicated website with a subscribe form, newsletter branding , and want to leverage features like a referral program, you should probably look into other newsletter platforms. There’s a trend in successful Substack newsletters migrating off the platform to tools like beehiiv and MailerLite to avoid revenue fees and more control over their subscriber list. ### 7. Mailmodo Mailmodo is a fairly new email marketing platform that allows you to create interactive emails that can make you seriously stand out from other newsletters. This tool is a bit more technical than the ones we’ve previously mentioned, however it is a great tool if you want to create totally custom email experiences for your subscribers. Backed by Y Combinator, the prestigious Silicon Valley venture firm, Mailmodo gives you a full WYSIWYG style editor that lets you build AMP and HTML email templates. There are also tons of other email marketing campaign features like automations, conversion tracking, surveys and quizzes you can use your emails , and other features that help gamify your newsletter. This truly is a great tool if you're familiar with no-code platforms and want to create a totally custom user experience for your newsletter. Just note that there may be a slight learning curve because it is a fairly powerful tool. Setting up your newsletter may not be as intuitive as the other email newsletter tools mentioned on this list. But, Mailmodo is extremely feature-rich and there is no other newsletter platform like it on this list. #### Mailmodo pricing Mailmodo’s pricing is quite generous for all the features it includes. Here are their pricing plans: Mailmodo follows a similar SaaS pricing models as beehiiv, MailerLite, and Kit. Their pricing increases with the number of subscribers you have. Here are their plans: - Lite: $39/month (billed annually), up to 2,500 subscribers with standard email sending features - Pro: $79/month (billed annually), starts at 2,500 subscribers with up to three team members - Max: $159/month (billed annually), starts at 2,500 subscribers with up to five team members They also have an enterprise option if you need a custom plan. ### 8. AWeber AWeber is an email marketing tool that has been around for some time now. It has established itself as a reliable platform to create and send emails. AWeber gives you the functionality of a newsletter platform, along with features like a landing page builder and email automation. You can create workflows for new subscribers and send them different types of newsletters to get them familiar with some of your best work. AWeber also has subscriber forms. So if you already have a website, you can easily send subscribers from your website straight to your AWeber

So if you already have a website, you can easily send subscribers from your website straight to your AWeber list. There’s also an ecommerce functionality, so you can sell digital products and services through transactional emails. AWeber also has a great email marketing blog if you're interested in learning more about email marketing. #### AWeber pricing AWeber’s pricing structure is simple like other platforms on this list. You can get started with AWeber for free, and only pay when you exceed 500 subscribers on your list. Here is how AWeber’s pricing works: Similar to MailerLite and Kit, AWeber’s pricing increases as you add on more subscribers to your email list. Here is what the pricing looks like for different subscriber tiers: - Free: $0/month, up to 500 subscribers, and includes most features - Lite: $15/month, starts at 500 subscribers, removes AWeber branding, and includes automations - Plus: $30/month, starts at 500 subscribers and higher sending volume - Unlimited: $899/month, up to 150,000 subscribers As you can see, a Plus plan can range from $30-$1,050 a month depending on how many subscribers you have. ### 9. Campaign Monitor Similar to AWeber, Campaign Monitor is an email marketing service that allows you to collect email addresses and send newsletters. This tool is great for small businesses that already sell products and services, but are looking to create content via a newsletter. Campaign Monitor has an easy to use drag-and-drop email builder, along with different email templates to customize your newsletter. You can also use automation workflows to send different newsletters to different sets of subscribers. Campaign Monitor also has tools like SMS marketing and ecommerce, which is why it’s probably best to use this tool as your newsletter platform only if you already have an existing business. If you just plan on creating a newsletter business, you’re better off using beehiiv, MailerLite, Substack, or Revue. #### Campaign Monitor pricing Similar to most of the email marketing-first platforms we’ve gone over, Campaign Monitor’s pricing varies based on the number of email subscribers you have. There is a free trial, but you’re going to have to pay regardless of what plan you choose. Here are Campaign Monitor’s pricing tiers: Each plan shown only gives you up to 500 subscribers. The plan tiers are based on the types of features you want. To be honest, their Basic plan will give you everything you need to start a newsletter. If you decide to just use the Basic plan, here is what the pricing would look like for different subscriber tiers: - Lite: $12/month at 500 subscribers - Essentials: $29/month starts at 500 subscribers with unlimited email sends - Premier: $159/month starts at 500 subscribers with advanced link tracking features As you can see, pricing can get hefty. However, if you’re a beginner just starting a newsletter from zero subscribers, you may want to consider some of the other newsletter platforms mentioned earlier. ### 10. Mailchimp Mailchimp is arguably the most popular email marketing and newsletter platform. At its core, Mailchimp is a marketing CRM that is focused on email. It can be used for all types of email campaigns, newsletter’s included. Mailchimp is quite overkill if you just want to launch a newsletter. But, because of its popularity, there are lots of resources and integrations available to make it an easy platform to use if you already have a website. Similar to Campaign Monitor, Mailchimp is a good newsletter platform if your business is more than just a newsletter. If you already sell different products or services, Mailchimp can be a good option to use as your email marketing platform. This is because you’ll be able to automate different parts of your email marketing strategy outside of just a newsletter. But you’ll also be able to create a newsletter on top of all the other email marketing automation stuff — hope that makes sense. It kills two birds with one stone if you plan on utilizing email marketing for more than just a content-driven newsletter. #### Mailchimp’s pricing Mailchimp has changed their pricing a lot of the years. At the time of writing this, you can start using the platform for free (up to 500 subscribers). And their Standard plan, regardless of how many subscribers you have, is free for the first month. Here is what Mailchimp’s pricing looks like for each plan: For some reason, Mailchimp’s pricing page reads from right to left — not common in other newsletter platform pricing models. Regardless, their free plan gives you most of the features you need to launch a newsletter. Paying extra will help you remove Mailchimp branding and get access to other features like A/B testing subject lines, behavioral targeting, custom templates, and advanced list segmentation. Assuming you go with their most popular “Standard” plan, here is what the pricing would look like for different subscriber counts: - Free: $0/month up to 500 subscribers (limited email marketing features) - Essentials: $13/month starting at 500 subscribers - Standard: $20/month starting at 500 subscribers - Premium: $350/month starting at 10,000 subscribers Mailchimp’s pricing is a standard amongst most email marketing platforms. Similar to some of the other platforms on this list, I only recommend Mailchimp if you are either just starting a newsletter as a test or if you want to leverage email marketing for other parts of your business.

Once our newsletter started growing, we decided to switch to a more newsletter-first platform like beehiiv. If you do want to use Mailchimp because of its features, but the pricing is a bit too much, you should also check out GetResponse or Constant Contact — they are great Mailchimp alternatives. Don’t get me wrong, Mailchimp is an amazing platform for email marketing (one of the best). But it does include a lot of features that you may not need if you just want to launch a newsletter. ## What is the best email newsletter platform right now? Out of all the platforms on the market today, the best email newsletter platforms right now (in my opinion) would have to be beehiiv, Ghost, or MailerLite. beehiiv is the platform I use for my newsletter and I absolutely love it. And no, they did not pay me to say that. I actually discovered them earlier this year when I learned that my favorite finance newsletter was using them. beehiiv is such a user-friendly and intuitive platform — it blew me away when I started using it. But the main thing that sold me was its attention to growth. The founders literally grew one of the largest business newsletters in the world, and saw how difficult and expensive it was to operate a newsletter that was built via custom solutions. Most large newsletters cost thousands of dollars a month just to keep up and running. And the fact that beehiiv lets you have 100,000 subscribers for just $100 a month is unheard of amongst any other newsletter platform. A very close second to beehiiv would have to be Ghost. This platform has evolved so well over the years, and to now see the team building it with a focus on newsletters is quite refreshing. Ghost is an amazing platform for newsletters and for websites that have a blog. To be honest, I probably would use Ghost if I did not build my website with Webflow . Webflow already has an incredible CMS and it’s what I use for my blog posts (including this one). But if I had to start all over, and build a media website from scratch, there’s a good chance I would pick Ghost to handle all of my content. Lastly, I would recommend MailerLite . If you don’t need the CMS and blog functionality that Ghost has, MailerLite is probably the best alternative to beehiiv at the moment. Their free plan is generous and they offer a lot of features that beehiiv currently doesn’t have. MailerLite is also a viable alternative to Ghost because it actually has a free plan. I actually discovered MailerLite after I already started growing on beehiiv, but there could have been a chance that I would have gone with MailerLite if I had discover it first. I actually use MailerLite for a different website that I run and I love it. It’s very hard to pick between beehiiv and MailerLite as a newsletter-only platform. ## Technical Comparison of LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI ### 🟨 1. CrewAI (Task-based, role-driven framework) Core components: Agent: Has a name, role, and tools (functions it can use) Task: Describes what the agent should accomplish Crew: A container managing a group of agents working on a shared objective #### 🔄 Execution Flow: Define each agent with a prompt template, tools, and role. Assign specific tasks to agents. Agents execute their tasks sequentially or in parallel, returning structured results. #### ⚙️ Example (Code writing crew): crew = Crew( agents=[Researcher, Coder, Reviewer], tasks=[ Task(agent=Researcher, description="Research Python sorting algorithms"), Task(agent=Coder, description="Write the code based on research"), Task(agent=Reviewer, description="Review and optimize the code"), ] ) result = crew.run() #### ✅ Strengths: Very easy to implement real-world workflows. Supports parallel agent execution. Minimal boilerplate. #### ⚠️ Limitations: Less control over state, memory, and loops. Not ideal for dynamic routing or complex logic. ### 🟦 2. AutoGen (Conversational agent framework) #### 🔍 Architecture: Core components: AssistantAgent, UserProxyAgent, GroupChat, OpenAIWrapper, etc. Agents are conversational — they communicate by sending messages back and forth. Built with an LLM messaging loop structure (like chain-of-thought). #### 🔄 Execution Flow: Define agents with prompts and behavior settings. Create a GroupChat with multiple agents. Trigger a loop — each message is passed and replied to based on logic. #### ⚙️ Example (Self-coding loop): coder = AssistantAgent("Coder", llm_config=...) critic = AssistantAgent("Critic", llm_config=...) chat = GroupChat(agents=[coder, critic]) chat.run("Write a function to reverse a list.") #### ✅ Strengths: Best for dynamic reasoning tasks. Agents “debate” or iterate until consensus is reached. Flexible agent personas. #### ⚠️ Limitations: Harder to control execution flow. Difficult to integrate tools and stateful memory. ### 🟩 3. LangGraph (Stateful, graph-based orchestrator) #### 🔍 Architecture: Core components: Node: A function (e.g., an LLM agent or tool). Graph: A Directed Cyclic Graph (DCG) of nodes and edges. State: Tracks intermediate data, variables, and control decisions. #### 🔄 Execution Flow: Define nodes (AI functions). Connect them with transitions (edges). Use state to persist memory across nodes. Define retry/loop/conditional logic per node. #### ⚙️ Example (Review workflow with retry): def ask_user(state): ... def generate_code(state): ... def review_code(state): ... builder = StateGraph(input_type=..., output_type=...) builder.add_node("ask_user", ask_user) builder.add_node("generate_code", generate_code) builder.add_node("review_code", review_code) builder.set_entry_point("ask_user") builder.add_edge("ask_user", "generate_code") builder.add_edge("generate_code", "review_code") builder.add_conditional_edges("review_code", check_quality) graph = builder.compile() output = graph.invoke(user_input) #### ✅ Strengths: Full control over flow, memory, and logic. Excellent for production-grade multi-agent applications. Re-entrant: allows retries, validation, and looping. #### ⚠️ Limitations: Steeper learning curve.
